utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would invite the parties to first discuss because, Mr. Kehoe, with all due respect, of course, you couldn't give evidence on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, I invite you to first briefly discuss the matter with Mr. Russo and to see whether there are any specifics in relation to this church which would assist the Chamber in evaluating this document in relation also to the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move a bit further down the target list, you will notice that the target which is third from the bottom is hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I'll ask you the same question, Colonel Konings, given your training and experience, whether or not you believe it is appropriate to include a hospital, any hospital, on a target list.

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A short answer, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would move for the admission of 65 ter 6119.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just I have been told by Mr. Misetic on something in this that the translation is off. I'm not really clear if I can turn to Mr. Misetic to clarify this. I don't speak the language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think OTP needs to revise the translation. The coordinates for each of the targets are one off, and early in the list somebody when they were transposing the numbers in the English missed one and then misnumbered all the rest of them as a result. So I think it needs to be fixed -- the translation needs to be fixed by OTP before it can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could, we're not admitting it for the coordinates, we're admitting it for the hospital being on the target list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The coordinate will be important later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Coordinates might be of importance because if the coordinates attached to the hospital would be coordinates which cannot be in any way -- as a matter of fact, I had on my mind to ask this witness about what the coordinates would mean here because we have usually in a -- in a flat country you usually need two coordinates. Now it seems that coordinates approximately the same appear under Z which suggests that that might be elevation, for example. Is that correctly understood, Mr. Konings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is correctly understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the target coordinates here, is that a grid system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that this is a grid system. It might be a different grid system than we use in NATO, but in the basis they are all the same. They give you an accuracy of the target up to either a single metre or ten metres or 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's dependent on the -- how many digits we have.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, whether you use ten digit or eight digit or six digit, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that the Defence will pay further attention to the target coordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I don't have to ask any further questions in --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's fine. I don't see why that would prevent the original B/C/S document from coming into evidence. We will simply revise the translation as we have done for others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's not even a translation matter. I do understand, but it is just a matter of putting the right numbers at the right places. May I take it there is no objection against this document as such if the English version is adjusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, could you please assign a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours this becomes Exhibit P1271.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1271 is admitted into evidence but still needs a better translation to be uploaded. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could now have 65 ter 6210.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You'll see, Colonel Konings, at the top here this indicates artillery preparation and the duration being 60 minutes, and you have already offered some testimony to the Chamber about what exactly artillery preparation fire is. And I'd like to look at the targets for artillery preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we can move down to the fourth line there, the -- the second from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You will see one target listed as a block of flats, and I would like you to please comment for the Chamber on whether or not you believe that's an appropriate thing to list on a target with no further information?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, that's pure speculation without giving the witness these grid references so that he can find it himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The grid references are there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, Mr. Russo, there is further specifications, the specifications being the references, apparently the grid references or the coordinates. Now, I don't think it makes much sense to ask this question as if -- I mean a block of flats could house everything, isn't it? So in order as to -- whereas earlier we had no opportunity to better understand what was fired at, here there may be a possibility at least if we do understand the coordinates, to find out whether this block of flats was housing civilians or military offices or police offices. So, therefore, I don't think that it makes much sense to ask whether the description as such which is accompanied by apparently clear grid references whether that would be acceptable or non-acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In that case, I will simply move to the next page -- actually the third page of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, has the Prosecution been able to identify the exact locations here, so that we would know what we might like to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That will be provided, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then we may know more than we do now. Please proceed. Yes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One other issue just considering -- pardon me, Judge, with regard to this document my understanding is that the Office of the Prosecutor has a copy of this document without the redactions that we just saw, the black lines through it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as a matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It was the page we had just before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the previous page. Do you have a copy without redactions Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I will check if we do, Your Honour. I'm not sure that those are actually redactions. They may, in fact, be highlighted things which were copied. In any case, we will pull out the original and determine whether or not we can upload something that doesn't have those markings on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I don't actually know if the original contains that or not, but I will pull it out of the evidence locker and determine that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would try to find such a copy and upload it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could magnify the English version a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Again, the second target listed you'll notice, Colonel Konings, is a hospital, and I take it that your opinion with respect to the appropriateness of including this on the target list remains the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, Judge. I objects if we're taking about the grid references, let's clarify the grid references. I think we have the witness's answer concerning theoretically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would not expect the Chamber to change his mind as far as hospitals should appear or not. I mean it was a superfluous question. But again, Mr. Russo, here we have - at least it appears to me - that there may be an opportunity to really identify in the field what we're talking about, and therefore if it is a hospital then we might find out whether it's a hospital which is still functioning or whether it's a building which was used 20 years ago as hospital and is still called a hospital or whether it is the hospital and then what location exactly --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wouldn't that be a more useful way of using this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Certainly we will connect this up with further evidence to establish to the Court where this particular hospital is located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But may I take it that you have already made an effort and have already attempted to find out which hospital this would have been?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I don't want to offer that testimony myself and this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it has been done so you know at least have you an impression for yourself on -- that this was really a hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Outside the presence of the witness, I would like to discuss that particular issue that these grid references have been brought up by the Office of the Prosecutor, and it is in fact a hospital in those grid references. I would like a good faith basis for at that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I -- as a matter of fact, what I would like -- the parties to do is to sit together and see whether they agree on the system of coordinates used here, and also to briefly discuss whether they come to the same conclusions apparently -- you have formed an opinion about that, Mr. Russo. Because if the parties would agree that X 79300, Y 97140, and Z 230 is a specific location, why not agree on that? Why not present it to the Chamber so that the Chamber can either understand or perhaps not understand what we're talking about. I mean, Mr. Russo --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm happy to do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because the witness can't help us out from what I understand. Yes? Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would still move for the admission of 65 ter 6120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And on the assumption that you upload a fully legible original. There are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As long as we have those redactions, we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that becomes Exhibit P1272.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1272 is admitted into evidence. But the OTP will take care that -- that a legible original will be uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have just been informed that those are in fact highlights, so we can upload a more legible version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could now have 65 ter 6128.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Colonel Konings, this is a coded map which lists various kinds of information in the tables, and the tables that -- which you see on there, one of them includes the list of targets identified on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could have the English translation of this brought up. And if we could move to page 8 of the English translation. And, again, Your Honour, I will simply make the proffer that this was a map which was received by the Office of the Prosecutor in response to a request for documents from the Croatian military archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, you will see on this target list, Colonel Konings, you'll notice targets 10, 11, and, I believe, 28 list medical stations, and I'd like your opinion, again in light of your training and experience, as to the appropriateness of including medical stations on targets, what you were taught about that and in fact what you teach to others about the appropriateness of targeting medical stations.

utterances.speaker: HARRY KONINGS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, my answer can be very short. First of all, it doesn't indicate whether it is a military medical station or a civilian medical station, but basically it doesn't care, because also military medical stations are designated units, designated parts of the military organisation, that should not be targeted. Wounded people are treated there, so they should not be targeted and definitely not be on the list of targets for artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, this map is from 1993. It was for a training exercise in 1993 and has nothing to do with Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that's the Defence's position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then you can -- I don't think, as a matter of fact, that there's any -- if that is relevant, and it may well be relevant, and not to say that sometimes maps keep validity, sometimes not, that's all to be established, it certainly will assist the Chamber in receiving more information about this map. And, of course, to the extent that the parties can agree on that, it's a map that was made in 1993, I've got no idea yet on where --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the title of the map is Poskok 93. I'm certainly willing to accept the fact and certainly agree to the fact that it may have been created for an exercise in 1993. However, we have received additional evidence from the government of Croatia which indicates that this map was in fact used in Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then share that information with the Defence, see to what extent you do agree, you do disagree, and then the Chamber would like to have the matter further explored during the presentation of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. We have provided the diary which indicates that this map was used that was provided to the Defence, I believe, on 26 November by e-mail but that is besides the point. I'm happy to get together with the Defence to discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I just have a -- I don't know if it -- two issues concerning this and also the questions along this line, if I could bring it outside the presence of the witness, I would appreciate it, as we come close to the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Konings, Mr. Kehoe would like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm happy to break here for the day, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Okay. Mr. Konings, we have to stay for another few minutes but you're free to go, but not after I have instructed you not to speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow, the 15th of January, quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom, number I.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I would also like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we raise other issues, I'm just trying to -- you said that it was page what of the translation page?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Page 8 is where this appears of the English translation of the map, Your Honour, if that's what the Court is asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I'm asking. And, as a matter of fact, in the original, it is a one-page document. So I have difficulties to find in the original where we see what is found in the list of targets in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If the Court can see the map, you will see that there are several boxes of text in the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which one is it, Mr. Russo?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not exactly sure. I believe it's one that is not currently on the screen; it's on the right-hand side of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, we have more there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And it's these which have been translated, including the text which appears at the top of the map. All of that is translated into the pages of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just trying to find it. Oh, yes, I think I found it at the -- yes, at the right-hand top. It's the one on the right-hand side the second from the top that table, yes. Thank you. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... with regard to this map, and I think you just saw that it said 1993 on the map, just scroll down on there, I think it was over on the right-hand side we saw that, we do know that it is not during the time of Operation Storm. Whether or not it was used as a basis thereafter, I'm not clear. But in the upper left-hand side, it will show the rank of General Gotovina as a brigadier and certainly at the time of Operation Storm he was not. And I do seem to think, as we were going through this, I did see a date of 1993 at some juncture. I think the larger issue here -- and there it is, 1993 in the right-hand corner. The larger issue here, Judge, is this, and that has to do with this expert testimony. There has been no testimony whatsoever that the HV targeted medical facilities in some school or anywhere else, and to put before this Chamber the fact that there is something on a list with grid references when, in reality, those facilities weren't targeted is completely misleading, and it is misleading to this witness. Now, to lead this witness to believe with this grid coordinates that the Knin hospital was shelled, we know, based on all of the Canadian witnesses and UN witnesses that have come in here, and there have been many, that it wasn't shelled. That it wasn't shelled at all. Yet Mr. Russo is putting forth items to this witness as if it had, and it is -- as a matter of fact, we all know that it had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is argument. I'm not sure where this is going. If this is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... because of the good faith effort of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, don't speak at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: May I add something, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me just ... if you add something and then I will give an opportunity to Mr. Russo to briefly respond, and I would like to keep this within certain time-limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. If we look at page 98, line 12, in the question in the transcript, it says: "Now, will you see on this target list, Colonel Konings, targets 10, 11 and 28," and if you enlarge the map -- and they're presented as being medical stations. There's nothing in those points in the map that lists these things as medical stations. It says: "Stacionar u skoli." That has nothing to do with medical stations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems, then, to be a translation issue. It says then station, school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And without the word medical, from what I understand. Let me -- I have to find my way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: 10 and 11 are "stacionar u skoli"; and 28 just says "stacionar."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to enlarge that to see whether I can follow. Mr. Russo, there seems to -- there may be a translation issue here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if there is a translation issue, we will certainly have it corrected. However, I believe on the whole target list there are, in fact, several entries for medical stations. We will certainly revise the translation, as appropriate. I may have called off the wrong numbers. But, that aside, I'm not sure what the Court wants me to respond to. I'm not sure if this is an objection to this particular exhibit that Mr. Kehoe was making or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'll clarify the objection. My objection is the good faith basis of questions concerning artillery attacks on a hospital when the Prosecutor knows that those the grid coordinates are not grid coordinates on the Knin hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it would be on another hospital, it might be relevant as well. But, therefore, I think I -- we don't have to decide the matter because we invited you to sit together and to see to what extent you can agree on what these coordinates or grid references, in whatever system, mean. If you cannot reach an agreement then, of course, the Chamber would like to hear what the issue is, why one party is relying on a system which apparently does not -- is in line with the other system, but let's first try to see whether we can get as close as possible to the facts on the basis of specific information we find in the material which is offered in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to add that Mr. Russo was very specific about points 10, 11, and 28. In the translation, it says medical station; in the original, it says nothing about a medical station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think, as a matter of fact, we established that, that it was "stacionar u skolu" and on 28 only "staciona." Now we have to find out whether this has a specific meaning. That is still possible even it's -- and why it is translated as it is translated. You're invited to first seek verification for the translation. Perhaps you also already include, Mr. Russo, those references for medical institutions or medical stations which you referred to but of which we do not know the number yet so that we don't end up in a similar situation tomorrow. And as far as the suggestions are concerned, you're invited - but then not with Mr. Kuzmanovic but now with Mr. Kehoe - to see what progress you can make on the coordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I will be moving 65 ter 6128 into evidence, but I do want to address the objection to the extent -- I'm not sure about the good faith basis portion of the objection. But where the witness indicates that putting something on a target list or something appearing on a map, whether or not it happens to be fired at is immaterial to the question. It is relevant to the determination of intent. Placing something on a target list establishes what the intent may be with respect to the attack in general. It doesn't certainly need to be proven that an artillery projectile actually hit that particular target, and we, of course, have already seen a report that projectiles were, in fact, fired at the Knin. Whether they hit the hospital or not is immaterial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll -- that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I respond just briefly. Then that raises an interesting point that the Prosecutor knows full well when he went into the Knin church, that was the St. Anthony's Monastery, a Catholic church that had been destroyed by the Serbs prior to Operation Storm, and that was never told to this witness by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct. It was never told to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's exactly right. It makes a big difference [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... it's irrelevant, Your Honour. It's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Oh my God.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The point of the witness's testimony was that a church on the target list --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think, as a matter of fact, you need this evening, the two of you, and then tomorrow we'll see where we are, and then we also have given an opportunity to our transcriber to recover from this event. And, Mr. Kehoe, I do understand the link but to say, Oh my God, and then specifically in relation to churches, and even in this context seems not to be the appropriate way of addressing --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn, and we'll -- I apologise for the interpreters and transcribers and everyone else who witnessed the last ten minutes, and we'll resume tomorrow, 15th of January, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of January, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.10 p.m.,
